links.reason: Kural 9 has எண்குணத்தான் (eight qualities); 961 has எண்வினை (eight karmas). The only tie is the number eight, and the verse does not name the Kural's figure, so reading it as 'filling' the epithet is a stretch.

2770 is about those who kill beasts and fish (கொலைநரை); Kural 255 is about those who eat flesh (ஊனுண்ண). The verse neither mentions eating nor adds anything to the rule, so it only illustrates hell for killing.

2451 has the ornaments cry that Death has come and 2452 has the fans and parasol hide the girl; this is story sequence, and the sense of அருளிலார் இவடம் அரன்னராயினும் is unclear, so 'answer to the danger' is a plot reading.

Line 1 அருளொடு படர்தல் செய்யாது ஆருயிர்க்கு அழிவு செய்து shows the king's own lament for killing; the Kural has no motive clause for the verse to add to, so 'adds the motive of greed' is the poem's illustration, not a qualification.

The Tamil really shares புள்ளுறு புன்கண் தீர்த்தோன் with Purananuru 37 line 5 (புள்ளுறு புன்கண் தீர்த்த), but the epic draws on a common legend, not on that poem; 'develops' overstates it, and the poem's own point (the same king is merciless in war) is not engaged.

Both verses name the goddess's place of slaughter, but 145 says nothing of the cock 'crying out'; the claimed shift from victims to substitute is the marker's, so this is a plot callback with an overreaching teaches.

Both liken women on high mansions to peacocks on a hill (Cintamani line 3 குன்றின் மேல் குழீஇய மஞ்ஞை; Perumpanarruppadai 330-331 மால்வரைச் சிலம்பின் ... மஞ்ஞையின்). The 'perfume smoke as mist' difference is visible, but the verse does not show it is traced to the older poem.

Line 4 of 323 has a voice from the branches say சீவ, and 361 line 4 names the child சீவகன்; the name answers the blessing. The 'mother' identification rests on other verses, but the link itself is borne out by the Tamil.

215 says a prior destiny (முனம் ஆகிய பான்மை) drove the king; 358 has a minister say fate decides outcomes of plans (ஊழது விளைவு) and still advise. They do not make incompatible claims about the same thing, and 215's narrator does not use fate as an excuse.

Both put Krishna similes on a man facing a beast, but 984 has the elephant (குஞ்சரம்) and Kalittokai 103 lines 53-55 have the horse; the 'bride-winning feat' pattern and the girl choosing are not in 984, and there is no sign of dependence.
1783 is a herald's call and the sound of conches and drums (சங்கொலி பரந்தன, மாமுரசு); it has no wedding-turned-funeral, so Naladiyar 23's மணப்பறை/பிணப்பறை warning is imported onto a neutral scene.

37 sets the bearer against the rider; 972 says birth is alike and distinction comes from செய்தொழில். They are not incompatible: both place difference in deeds, and 972 qualifies a birth-rank reading of 37.

1370 has her strip her bracelets for hindering the embrace (கூடப் புல்லிவை யாக்குற்றம்); it is a scene of union, not separation, and வாடடினாள் looks miscopied, so Kural 1157's slipping bangle as sign of parting is not the same thing.

338 compares body and life parting to a bird leaving the nest; 2754 says a child may die in the womb like a bubble (மொக்குளு மென). The only tie is that life is fragile; the verse has no nest and does not extend the couplet.

56 says that with no enemies the king guards himself and the earth; 67 says the queens draw his mind from ruling. The first makes no claim that the second contradicts, and the marker notes the narrator does not blame anyone.

1286 lists eight causes of snakebite (எட்டினாகும்) and kinds of bite, which does match 948's order of finding disease and cause. But the 'rival healers who fail' that the teaches rests on are in other verses, so the pair is an illustration.
252 says the longing ended (வயாநோய் தீர்ந்து) and the prince is born; 243 has the longing begin. This is plot sequence, and 'easy birth' and 'god's help' are not in 252.

1850 is the body's foulness (முடையு நீரு ... அழுகல்) and the Thiruppugazh also describes it; the Jain king's plan to leave is not in 1850, and the Thiruppugazh's grace plea is a different Tamil school's exit. The shared catalogue is the only link.

166's line 4 (தாஞ்சுவை திரிந்த பின் இன்றைச் சார்பவர் இல்லை) adds that followers leave when sweetness turns, which Naladiyar 160 (உடையார் இவரென்று ... பின்சென்று வாழ்வார்) does not say. But 160's real point is lineage as treasure, so the pair is thin.

Both use கயிறு with ஆர்க்கும்/நல்வினை, but the ropes are different (one binds the false practiser, the other holds merit); Thirikadugam says nothing about sincerity, so the 'turns on sincerity' teaching is the marker's.

Both use the drum image: Kural 1180 அறைபறை கண்ணார் and 1963 பறையா யறையும் பசப்பு. The skin-and-eyes pairing is true, but 'at first sight' is not in the verse, and the body-betrays-secret reading is thin.

Kural 29 is about the anger of those on the hill of good qualities, and its meaning is disputed; 2107 compares speed to கடவுளர் வெகுளி (gods' anger) and states no source, so 'an early reader's construal' is invented.

Both use the umbrella (குடையின் நீழலார், கவிகைக்கீழ்த் தங்கும் உலகு), but 596 says nothing of bitter words; the 'what keeps them there' is imported from the Kural and the stock umbrella image carries the link.

143 has the king say no one can turn back ripening deeds; 144 shows him consenting anyway (பற்றறத் துணிவில் மன்னன்). That is a claim and the act that undercuts it, more develops than tension, and both verses are flagged as uncertain.

513 has the sea swallow his wealth (ஓம்பிப் படைத்த பொருள்) and Sitattan stand calm; merit and its exhaustion are not in the verse, so the 'cause' is imported from Naladiyar 93 (விடுக்கும் வினையுலந்தக்கால்).
Both name two deeds (இருவினை), but Naga 20 says the lord declared them (பகர்ந்தாய்); it does not say the teaching frees, as Kural 5 says praise does. The shared word is the only tie.
692 has the soldiers recall Civakan's feeding them, matching Kural 226's hunger relief; the fear he causes the usurper is in 693, not here, so the 'return as danger' teaching rests on another verse.

Both have the lotus-walker (விரைமணந்த தாமரைமேல் ... சென்றாய், மலர்மிசை ஏகினான்), a real shared image. But the Kural does not gain a worship scene from this, and reading its Lord as the Arhat is one contested view.
32 has clouds drink from the sea (கலங்கு தெண் திரை மேய்ந்து) which Kural 17 treats as a debt to be repaid; but 32 states no repayment, and the sea-to-sea ordering is not shown to enact the couplet.
35 lists his elephant-taming and flawless veena (மறுவில் வீணை); 48 shows him playing it. The trap is not in 48's Tamil, so 'the skill is his weak point' is plot knowledge, and the link is plot order.

2084 has her refuse a chest 'many embrace' (பலர்முயங் கார மார்பின்) as Kural 1311 has the woman refuse because all feast on him with their eyes (பரத்த நின் மார்பு). The epic gives the oodal pretext a real base: Civakan already has several wives, which is a true qualification.

TM 203 says even the learned and the yogis fall for bewildering women (மாதர் மயலுறுவார்கள்); Yasodhara 96 is about a queen's desire. The gender is reversed and she is not shown learned or a yogi, so 'a case of a general weakness' is loose.
links.text_issue: TM 203 line 3 கொணட typo; Yasodhara 96 line 4 hard

links.reason: 1551 has lust, drink and meat (காமம் ... நறவு ... ஊன்) and 1234 has meat, honey and toddy (ஊனொடு தேனுங் கள்ளும்); the echo is real, but நறவு can be honey or toddy, so 'honey drops out' is not secure.

1879 has the girl ask her parrot whether tomorrow is near or far (நாளையெனும் நாள் அணிமைத்தோ ... சேய்த்தோ), a fair parallel to 1269. But the gains names Gunamalai, who is not the girl in this chapter, and 'makes it measurable' is not what the verse does.

304 says kings paid tribute out of fear (திறைகொடுத்து அறிவித்தன்று) and 663 begins a list of demands; this is plot order, and 304's own claim is about austerity, not tribute as a power the later verse enacts.
1667 has her send the garland (பிணிப்பேன் எனத் ... மாலை கொடுத்து) and 1670 has him take it (ஒலியல் ஏற்றான்); this is the next step in the plot, and 'hesitant consent' is not in 1670.

168 is about envy (அழுக்காறு) ruining fortune; 35 shows a new queen's suspicion and her prayer, with no envy shown. The pair share only the topic of rivalry, and the note itself says the verse does not show it.

Purananuru 20 says omen birds do not disturb the king (புதுப்புள் வரினும் பழம்புள் போகினும் ... ஏமக் காப்பினை); 2173 lists omens (கூகை ... பகற்குழறக்) in a palace. The poem does not say omens do strike others, so the 'counter-case' is imposed.

1732 and 1712 both end நம்பி தோன்றினான் with a radiant birth, a stock image; the marker says the 1732 boy is the queen's son while the note says a Vidyadhara boy, and 'set side by side as equals' is not in the Tamil.

445 has the priest foretell a Vidyadhara lord's coming for the king's son; 1015 has Madhavasenai bring a drawn form (உருவம்) to Tivittan. 1015 does not say the form is the girl's or that the prophecy is being fulfilled, so the link is a plausible plot step.

951 has the dog reborn a god after the five padas (கற்றவைம் பதங்கள் நீராக ... தேவனாகி), and 3036 has the words set at the ear of the dying (சாவா கிடந்தார் செவிச்சார்த்தின்) make them gods at once. The general rule at the close does cover the earlier case.

NAL 130 says the home bond is idle beside good done (செய்தநன்றல்லால் ... பயனில்லை), but the marker notes it does not call family a hindrance; so 'quatrain makes family a hindrance' is untrue, and 2728 has the family lost to sin, not spent as merit.

Both have the shoulders lose old beauty with slipping bangles (தொன்னலம் இழந்த ... ஞெகிழ vs தொல்கவின் வாடிய தோள் ... தொடி சோரும்); Ainkurunuru is the earlier poem, so it cannot 'develop' the Kural. The rains-timing is the poem's own addition.
